rows.title: The web platform — Rules
rows.summary: 1. The web platform is the mobile platform in a browser.
body: 1. **The web platform is the mobile platform in a browser.** A kind that exists on both has the same word and the
same rules; a kind is added here with the mobile platform's word, never a new one
([ADR-web-0001](docs/03-adr/0001-web-platform.md)).
2. **The platform names no dialect.** `docs/07-reference/web.md`, the brief, `platform.toml` and the `.nuc` of the
example hold only Nuclear and Nuclear's own library. How React writes a kind is in the dialect's reference.
3. **`platform.toml` is the contract.** A kind or a decorator a dialect uses is listed there, or the loader refuses
the dialect (N0305).
4. **No JSX.** A view returns elements made with the runtime's HTML functions; the parser does not change for a
dialect.
5. **A changed public API of the runtime** means its type definitions are regenerated
([runbook](docs/06-runbooks/change-the-runtime.md)).
6. **The example is a golden.** Output that changed on purpose: `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test`, then review the diff.
7. **A file's name in `docs/07-reference/` is its topic**: `nuclear help web` and `nuclear spec --brief` find them
by name, and the installer copies the folder with `platform.toml` and `packages/`. They are normative: changed
only with the feature they describe.
8. Done = `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and the check green, the reference and these documents

rows.title: The web platform
rows.summary: The web platform of Dragonfly: apps that run in the browser, written in Nuclear with the same words as the mobile platform.
body: The web platform of Dragonfly: apps that run in the browser, written in Nuclear with the same words as the mobile
platform. This folder holds what is the same for every dialect: the contract (`platform.toml`), the runtime package
the generated app runs on, the example and the check. The Nuclear of a web project never changes when its dialect
changes.
Paths in these documents are relative to this folder (`nuclear-synapsis-framework/platforms/web/`); a path that
starts with `nuclearlang/`, `nuclear-synapsis-framework/`, `tools/`, `installer/` or `.github/` starts at the root
of the tree. The rules of the whole platform are in [the root `AGENTS.md`](../../../AGENTS.md).

rows.title: Vision — Constraints
rows.summary: components (another component is used only through its `appcomponent`), with the same N0301 / N0302 rules as the mobile platform.
body: - The golden rule of the whole platform: performance, speed and readability of the syntax.
- A light clean architecture: `data`, `domain` and `presentation` layers plus what is shared, and closed
components (another component is used only through its `appcomponent`), with the same N0301 / N0302 rules as the
mobile platform.
- The http client with cache and retries, the state managers, events, session, ACL, the router and the test helpers
come from the dialect's runtime package; the UI library, the bundler and the test runner are the dialect's.

rows.title: Vision — The problem
rows.summary: Dragonfly names three platforms, and the web one is built on what the mobile platform already does, so the knowledge of one carries to the other.
body: Dragonfly names three platforms, and the web one is built on what the mobile platform already does, so the
knowledge of one carries to the other. The web platform is the mobile platform in a browser: the same words for the
same things (`appConfig`, `repository` with `@get`, `usecase`, `appcomponent`, state models and `statemanager`,
`@screen`, events, guards, tests), so an app's domain and state read the same on a phone and on the web, and a
person or an agent that knows one writes the other.
A web project holds only its business logic in Nuclear. Components, props, registration in the injector, JSON, http
calls, state handling, routes and imports are written by the transpiler.

rows.title: Vision — What it does not do
rows.summary: words with a mobile one (ADR-web-0001).
body: - It is not designed from a UI library up: no kind for a hook, a store or JSX. The Nuclear of a web app shares its
words with a mobile one ([ADR-web-0001](../03-adr/0001-web-platform.md)).
- It has no JSX: the parser does not change for a dialect. A view returns elements made with HTML functions.
- It does not navigate by address: `goTo` takes a screen, as on mobile.
- What a browser has no use for is not here (a native splash, workmanager, a secure keystore); what a browser needs
and a phone does not is (HTML elements, a url bar).
- It does not say how a dialect writes its target: that is the dialect's reference, in the TypeScript dialect
project.
- Not there yet ([roadmap](../01-product/roadmap.md)): forms, converters, translations, the local database, plugins
and AI kinds. They come with the mobile platform's words.

rows.title: Vision — Who uses it
rows.summary: (`nuclear help web`) and the brief.
body: - **A person or an AI agent writing a web app**: they read [the reference](../07-reference/web.md)
(`nuclear help web`) and [the brief](../07-reference/brief/web.md).
- **Whoever already has the mobile app**: the `characters` example here is the mobile one minus the widgets of the
mobile dialect.
- **The author of a dialect**: `platform.toml` says what a web dialect must implement.
- **Whoever changes the runtime** (`packages/dragonfly-web`): the code every generated app runs on.

rows.title: Architecture — From a project to an app in the browser
rows.summary: a web project (.nuc, config.nuc, public/) │ nuclear build . / dragonfly build ▼ the compiler ── loads ──► the dialect nuclearlang/dialects/typescript/frameworks/react/ │ └─ platform = "web" ──► platform.toml (this folder: the contract) ▼ build/app the dialect's app, never edited ── imports ──► the…
body: a web project (.nuc, config.nuc, public/)
│  nuclear build .  /  dragonfly build
the compiler ── loads ──► the dialect   nuclearlang/dialects/typescript/frameworks/react/
│                        └─ platform = "web" ──► platform.toml   (this folder: the contract)
build/app   the dialect's app, never edited ── imports ──► the runtime   (packages/dragonfly-web)
│        public/ copied as it is
the app in the browser: one route per screen
A project has only `.nuc` files and `public/`: `config.nuc` (`dragonfly(platform = "web", dialect = ...)`,
`app(...)`, `contracts(...)`, `dependencies(...)`), `main.nuc` (the App view: the router with every screen),
`config/project_config.nuc`, components with `config/`, `data/`, `domain/` and `presentation/`, `shared/`, tests in
`test/*_test.nuc`. The rules are [the reference](../07-reference/web.md).

rows.title: Architecture — The contract: `platform.toml`
rows.summary: The contract: `platform.toml`
body: | Section | In the web contract |

| `[platform]` | `default_dialect = "react"`. Kinds, the mobile platform's that make sense in a browser: `stateless`, `stateful`, `appConfig`, `config`, `repository`, `usecase`, `appcomponent`, `service`, `aggregate`, `statemanager`, `statemodel`, `model`, `component`, `guard`, `event`, `tests`. Decorators: http (`repository`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `path`, `query`, `body`), state (`stateModel`, `state`, `before`, `after`), screens, events and access (`screen`, `on`, `requires`, `acl`), tests (`mock`, `test`, `widget`, `states`) and `key`. No plugins |
| `[decorators.*]` | none |

| `[layout]` | a path per kind: `config/project_config.nuc`, `test/`, `shared/{components,guards,events}/`, and under `components/{component}/`: `config/`, `data/`, `domain/{models,usecases,services,aggregates}/`, `presentation/{screen}/` (views), `presentation/{screen}/managers/`, `presentation/{screen}/state_models/`, and the facade `{component}_component.nuc` |
| `[skeletons]` | `repository`, `model`, `usecase`, `service`, `appcomponent`, `statemodel`, `stateless`, `stateful`, `event`, `tests` |

rows.title: Architecture — What the `dragonfly` command does with a web project
rows.summary: The command is another project.
body: The command is [another project](../../../../../tools/cli/AGENTS.md). What it takes from here:
- `dragonfly new <name> -p web -d react` writes the skeleton of a project (`web_project` in
`nuclear-synapsis-framework/cli/src/scaffold.rs`).
- `build`, `install`, `run` and `test` go through the dialect's `[toolchain]`, and `check` runs `nuclear check .`,
as for backend projects (`non_mobile_manifest` in `nuclear-synapsis-framework/cli/src/main.rs`).
- `dragonfly make` reads `[layout]` and `[skeletons]`; `dragonfly gen resource` writes a resource's models,
repository, use cases, view and tests from the `[[generators.*]]` (ADR-codegen-0001).

rows.title: The runtime: `dragonfly-web` — Entry points and modules
rows.summary: Entry points and modules
body: | Import | Module | Holds |
| `dragonfly-web` | `result` | `Result`, `Ok`, `Err`: the same runtime the `typescript` dialect writes in a file and `dragonfly-nest` exports |
| | `errors` | `AppError` (Nuclear's `Error(message)`), `HttpError` (a failed request), `NotFound` |
| | `inject` | the injector: `register`, `replace`, `inject`, `isRegistered`, `resetInjector`. Singletons are built once; factories (use cases, managers) on every `inject` |
| | `config` | `AppConfig`, `ComponentConfig`, `Connection`, `Global`, the `Http` connection and `HttpInterceptor` |

rows.title: The runtime: `dragonfly-web` — How it is installed
rows.summary: An app gets the runtime as a copy, never as a link: from a link, TypeScript and Vite resolve the runtime's imports (`react`) next to the runtime's own folder, not the app's; the types become `any` and the bundle fails.
body: An app gets the runtime as a copy, never as a link: from a link, TypeScript and Vite resolve the runtime's imports
(`react`) next to the runtime's own folder, not the app's; the types become `any` and the bundle fails. After a
reinstall Vite's dependency cache is removed: it would keep serving the runtime it bundled before (same version,
new code). The dialect's `[toolchain] install` does both.

rows.title: The runtime: `dragonfly-web` — How the pieces work
rows.summary: (`goTo(CharacterDetailScreen, { id })`) from anywhere in a view.
body: - **Router.** One route per `@screen(route = "/path/:id")`, built by the transpiler; navigation is by screen
(`goTo(CharacterDetailScreen, { id })`) from anywhere in a view.
- **Session and access.** `SessionManager` keeps who is signed in; `Acl` the roles, permissions and guards;
`Guards` runs the checks a use case asks for (`@requires(session = true)`, `@acl(roles = [...])`).
`Guards.verify` is asynchronous.
- **Logs.** `Log` writes with the place it is called from; the transpiler passes it (component › kind ›
Class.method · file:line).
- **Tests.** `DragonflyTest` starts the app with its real config and replaces `fetch` by canned answers; any
registered class can be a mock (`when`, `verify`); `renderScreen` renders a screen with Testing Library;
`statesOf` collects the states a manager emits.

rows.title: The runtime: `dragonfly-web` — How the pieces work
rows.summary: `statefulOf`), so hooks work inside `build`.
body: - **Views.** A view is a class (`StatelessView` / `StatefulView`) shown through `createElement` (`statelessOf` /
`statefulOf`), so hooks work inside `build`. A `stateless` is built on every render; a `stateful` keeps its
instance, and so its fields, between renders and re-renders on `setState` (`initState`, `dispose`), the way the
mobile platform's stateful view does.
- **HTML without JSX.** `div({ className: 'row', children: [...] })`; a string, a number, an element or a list
given in place of the props is the children.
- **State.** A `StateManager` holds one state model and emits a new one; React reads it with
`useSyncExternalStore`. The same shape as the mobile platform's state manager. The dialect generates a
`<Model>Builder` component for each state model.
- **Providers.** `@screen(providers)` wraps the screen in `Providers`; `Manager.method()` inside its views is
`this.manager(Manager).method()`, which reads the provided manager without a hook, so it works in a callback.
`useManager` and `useStateOf` are hooks: only in `build`.
- **Repositories.** Each method is an http call through `send` (fetch), with the mobile platform's rules: the path
is appended to the connection's `baseUrl`, `:name` takes a parameter, the other parameters go to the query (GET,
DELETE) or the JSON body; a cache by key with a ttl; retries on transient failures.

rows.title: Testing — Conventions
rows.summary: every request answers what the test prepares; a class is a mock with `@mock`.
body: - **The tests of a project are written in Nuclear** (`tests` in `test/`): the app starts with its real config and
every request answers what the test prepares; a class is a mock with `@mock`. The words are the mobile
platform's (`@test`, `@states`, `@widget`).
- **The golden.** When the generated output changes on purpose: `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test`, then review the diff.
- **No browser.** The check ends at jsdom and a bundle; the app in a real browser is in the
[roadmap](../01-product/roadmap.md) as untested.

rows.title: Testing — Running the check
rows.summary: cargo test sh nuclear-synapsis-framework/platforms/web/checks/react-check/check.sh The script finds the tree from its own place (`NUCLEAR_ROOT` overrides it) and stops at the first failure.
body: ```sh
cargo test
sh nuclear-synapsis-framework/platforms/web/checks/react-check/check.sh
The script finds the tree from its own place (`NUCLEAR_ROOT` overrides it) and stops at the first failure. In
order:
1. Builds the runtime with `tsc` and copies it fresh into `nuclearlang/tools/node/node_modules`
(`npm install --no-save --install-links`). npm keeps an old copy of the same version, so the script removes it
first; a `--no-save` install also prunes the other runtime installed the same way, so the backend platform's
nestjs check installs its own again.
2. Builds `examples/examples-web/characters` (`cargo run -p nuclear-cli -- build`) and links `node_modules` into
its `build/app`.
3. `tsc --strict` over the generated app.
4. The example's own tests with vitest in jsdom (4 tests, written in Nuclear in `test/characters_test.nuc`).
5. `vite build`: a production bundle.
6. The runtime's tests, in `packages/dragonfly-web`.

rows.title: AGENTS.md — NuclearLang
rows.summary: This project is written in NuclearLang (`.nuc`), dialect `react`.
body: This project is written in NuclearLang (`.nuc`), dialect `react`. Its syntax is not TypeScript, Dart nor Python.
- Before writing code, read the sheet: `nuclear spec --brief --dialect react`.
- After each change: `nuclear check <file>.nuc --dialect react --json` must report no errors; fix exactly what each error says (most carry a `fix`).
- Look up instead of guessing: an API `nuclear defs show <Name> --dialect react`; a kind or decorator
`nuclear help <word> --dialect react` (all: `nuclear help words --dialect react`); a topic `nuclear help <topic>`.
- Never edit generated code (`build/` and the `.ts`/`.dart`/`.py` built from the `.nuc`): change the `.nuc` files.
<!-- /nuclearlang -->

rows.title: NuclearLang website — Build
rows.summary: (cd tools && npm install) # markdown-it, shiki and smol-toml, once node tools/content.mjs # the content, from the tree site.toml names ([source] tree; NUCLEAR_TREE overrides it) dragonfly build # the app into build/app (public/ copied) dragonfly install # npm install in build/app dragonfly test #…
body: ```sh
(cd tools && npm install)        # markdown-it, shiki and smol-toml, once
node tools/content.mjs           # the content, from the tree site.toml names ([source] tree; NUCLEAR_TREE overrides it)
dragonfly build                  # the app into build/app (public/ copied)
dragonfly install                # npm install in build/app
dragonfly test                   # vitest: the tests of test/
dragonfly run                    # vite dev, http://localhost:5173
(cd build/app && npx vite build) # the published site in build/app/dist
`tools/content.mjs` renders every page's markdown with the code already highlighted (shiki, with the Nuclear grammar
of the editors and their Chernobyl theme), so the browser receives HTML and never parses markdown. The home page's
sample is transpiled to TypeScript, Dart and Python by the installed `nuclear` when the site is built. For search
engines and agents that read without JavaScript, every page also has a plain HTML copy in `/static/` (and the
sitemap, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`).
The addresses are the paths of the repositories' files: `/docs/language/01-syntax` is `docs/language/01-syntax.md`.
A link between pages reloads the page (the content is cached by the browser); navigation by address inside the app is
a later step of the web platform.
